issues.description: Both the template and solution Dockerfiles reference a start.sh script (COPY start.sh, RUN chmod ... , CMD ./start.sh) but no start.sh file is present in the repository tree provided. The problem statement also instructs to copy and make start.sh executable. The missing start.sh is a structural omission that will prevent students from successfully building the Docker image as described and blocks following the deployment steps.
issues.suggestedFix: Add the start.sh script to the repository at the project root (matching the Dockerfile COPY path) and ensure it contains the expected startup command (e.g. java -jar app.jar). Alternatively, update the Dockerfile to use an ENTRYPOINT/CMD that does not rely on a missing start.sh, and reflect this change in the problem statement instructions so students can build the image as described.

issues.description: The template PersonResource.createPerson method returns a ResponseEntity<Person> (and returns the saved person), while the solution's PersonResource.createPerson has a void return type and simply calls personService.save(person). The problem statement describes REST endpoints but does not fix the return type. This mismatch in method signature between template and solution may confuse students when comparing their implementation to the provided solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the createPerson method signature consistent between template and solution. Either change the template to match the solution (void, call save without returning) or change the solution to return ResponseEntity<Person> with the saved entity. Also update the problem statement examples (if any) to reflect the chosen return behavior so students aren't confused by differing signatures.
